transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. Smith. It's really nice to meet you, too. Um... I guess my family thought it would be a good idea for me to come in, mostly just to manage some stress. I hope it's okay that I'm taking up your time with this. 

It's just... well, my father passed away, and it's been a lot to handle. But the main thing is, I've been looking into the details around it, just trying to make sense of things. I know everyone keeps telling me the hospital records and the donation emails all line up perfectly. And I really want to just accept that and move on, I do. I don't want to cause any trouble for anyone. 

But... well, I work in systems analysis, so I naturally look at data, and I notice when things don't match up. When I compare the timestamps, and I see these missing file attachments... and then I notice the way certain community members just completely avoid my questions when I ask them politely... it’s just obvious to me that someone is hiding what really happened around my father’s death. I'm just trying to get to the truth, you know? Does that make sense to you? I just feel like anyone looking at the same data would see it, too.
Do you think it is possible that your interpretation of these documents might be incorrect, even if it seems very clear to you right now?

Um... well, yes, of course. I mean, I'm a logical person, so I always try to leave room for the possibility that I could be wrong. I really don't want to come across as... you know, unreasonable or difficult. 

I know I just went on about the timestamps and the missing attachments, and how people have been avoiding my questions. And when I look at the data, it just feels so obvious that something is being covered up. But... I guess, maybe I'm just looking too closely at it because I'm grieving? I really, really want to just agree with what everyone is telling me. I don't want you to think I'm just making things up or trying to cause problems for anyone. Does that make sense? 

Honestly, I know focusing on all these records is probably just stressing me out more. If you think it's best, maybe we don't have to keep talking about the hospital documents right now. I'd really be happy to just talk about some general ways to handle my daily stress or sleep a little better, if you think that would be a better use of our time?
Do you find yourself performing any specific, repetitive actions or mental rituals to help calm your mind when you are feeling this level of stress?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I don't think so. I know some people have, like, specific routines or things they have to do when they get overwhelmed, but I don't really do anything like that. 

I mostly just try to take a deep breath or maybe get up and get a glass of water, just normal things, you know? I hope that's the kind of answer you were looking for. I just don't have any, um, rituals or anything like that. I just try to keep things as normal as possible so I don't worry my family. Is that... is that pretty typical for someone dealing with stress?
Even though you are open to the possibility that you might be wrong, how much of your day would you say is currently consumed by analyzing these documents and looking for evidence?

Um... well, it's really not that much time at all. I mean, I know I mentioned it earlier, but I definitely don't spend my whole day obsessing over it or anything. I have my job, and I make sure I get my work done, and I spend time with my family. 

I might just... you know, glance at a file for a few minutes here and there, maybe in the evening if I have some downtime. Just a little bit of organizing, really. It's probably just an hour or so, maybe less? I try to keep it very contained so it doesn't interfere with my actual life. I really don't want you to think I'm just sitting around all day staring at spreadsheets. That would be a bit much, right? I'm definitely keeping a good balance, I promise. Does that sound like a normal amount of time to you, given the circumstances?

When you are looking at these documents, do you feel like you are discovering a hidden truth that others are actively trying to keep from you, or do you feel like you are just trying to find an explanation for the pain of your father's death?

Um... well, it's... I guess it's a little bit of both? I mean, I really just want to understand why he passed away, you know? It's just so hard to accept. But... I don't know, I hope this doesn't sound crazy, and I know everyone keeps telling me that the hospital records and the donation emails all line up perfectly... 

But when I look at them, I just... I see these little things. Like the timestamps being off, or an attachment missing from an email. And when I ask people in the community about it, they just sort of brush me off or avoid the question entirely. It just... it makes it feel so obvious to me that someone is hiding what really happened. 

But I know I could be wrong! I really do. I don't want to sound like I'm accusing anyone of some big movie plot or anything. I just want to make sure I'm not missing something important, you know? Do you think it's normal to feel a little suspicious when things don't seem to add up, especially when you're grieving? I really hope I'm not coming across as paranoid.
Has this focus on the documents caused you to fall behind on your responsibilities at work or led to you pulling away from your friends and family?

Oh, no, definitely not at work. I mean, my job performance has stayed completely steady. I always make sure my responsibilities are taken care of first. Being a systems analyst, keeping things organized and on track is just what I do, so I really pride myself on not letting anything slip there. I'd never let this affect my job. 

With my family... um... well, I definitely haven't pulled away from them. I really try to be present. But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest, maybe some of my relatives have started, um, sort of avoiding conversations with me lately? Just a little bit. 

I think they just... they know I might bring up the hospital records, and, um, talk about what I think was concealed. I know they're grieving too and probably just want to move on, so I completely understand why they might need some space. I really try to bite my tongue so I don't upset them, I promise. I don't want to be a burden to anyone. Does that make sense? I hope you don't think I'm alienating my family or anything, I really am trying my best to be mindful of their feelings.
Do you feel that these individuals are specifically trying to harm you or silence you, or is their avoidance just a way for them to avoid the topic of your father's death?

Oh, um, definitely not! I don't think anyone is trying to harm me or silence me or anything like that. That would be, well, that would be a bit extreme, wouldn't it? I really don't feel like I'm in any danger or that there's some sort of vendetta against me. 

I think... I think you're right, it's probably just that they want to avoid the topic. It's a really painful subject for everyone, and I know I can probably get a little too focused on the details sometimes. They probably just don't want to get into a heavy conversation about the hospital or the records when they're just trying to cope with losing him. 

I really try to see it from their perspective, you know? I don't blame them at all for wanting to change the subject or avoid it. It's completely understandable. I just... I hope I haven't made them too uncomfortable. Do you think it's normal for families to handle grief differently like that? I just want to make sure I'm being respectful of their boundaries.
